# Micah Hoang Design System: for agents

The foundations, components and page patterns behind micahhoang.com, the portfolio of brand designer Micah Hoang. Everything is plain markdown; you never need to render the HTML site to read it.

## Where things are

| What | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Every page, one line each | `llms.txt` |
| Everything in one file (pages + tokens) | `llms-full.txt` |
| One page | `content/<section>/<slug>.md` |
| Components: classes, tokens, Framer ids | `components.json` |
| Tokens (source of truth, W3C DTCG) | `tokens/tokens.json` → `tokens/tokens.css` (generated) |
| Styles and behavior | `css/components.css`, `js/components.js` |
| What changed and when | `content/reference/changelog.md` |

Pages describe the current live site only. Component pages share one order: examples (```` ```html example ```` blocks you can copy), usage, API, accessibility, Framer mapping, don'ts.

## The brand in ten lines

1. Two surfaces: **Cream** `#F7F5F0` (default) and **Forest Green** `#233324` (footer, loader, mobile menu).
2. Two typefaces: **GT Standard** for display and reading, **GT Standard Mono** for every label, always uppercase, always 13px.
3. Display type is huge and tight (120px hero, 70px sections, 100% leading, -1% tracking); everything else is small. Phone reading text is 18px.
4. Flat: no shadows, gradients or rounded cards. Square media. The only radius is the tag pill.
5. Structure comes from **1px near-black rules** (`#141414`) and space, never boxes.
6. No filled button. Links and actions are mono text with a **flip** (420ms Snappy, one line up); pills are outlined.
7. Accent green `#25593A` is for hover/active only; Stroke Gray `#848484` (3.43:1) never for text someone must read.
8. Motion decelerates, moves a line or a few pixels, exits faster than it enters, and respects reduced motion.
9. A faint umber film grain sits over every page below the nav.
10. Voice: considered, quiet, alive, specific, shipped. "I did X", not "we did Y".

## Rules

- **Use what exists.** If a page documents it, reuse it. Most pieces already exist in Framer; check the page's Framer mapping (`codeFileId`, style name) before building anything.
- **Tokens, never raw values.** `var(--mh-…)` in code, the token's Framer style in Framer. Missing a value? Add it to `tokens.json` and run `node build.mjs`. Global values live in `layout`; per-component measurements in `component.<name>` (CSS `--mh-<name>-<key>`).
- **Semantic roles, not primitives.** `var(--mh-text-muted)`, not `var(--mh-color-light-gray)`; roles re-map inside `data-surface="green"`.
- **Breakpoints** 1200 / 810 / 390. **One 20px gutter** everywhere; **44px touch targets** below 810px (grow padding, not type).
- **Don't invent brand.** No new colors, fonts, radii, shadows, gradients, emoji or icon sets. Too plain? Use scale, space or real project media.
- **Don't change the live site from here.** [Principles](content/foundations/principles.md#interaction-rules) labels each interaction rule Already true / New work / Departure. Changing micahhoang.com needs Micah's approval, a pushed dated rollback branch (repo `AGENTS.md`) and a Framer publish.
- **`/play` is protected.** Its drag, inertia and video budget are performance contracts in the repo `AGENTS.md`.

## Quick start

HTML:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="css/fonts.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="tokens/tokens.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="css/type.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="css/base.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="css/components.css">
<body data-surface="cream">
  …
  <script src="js/components.js"></script>
</body>
```

Framer:

- Colors: `/Colors/` Cream, Forest Green, Off-Black, Text Gray, Stroke Gray, White. Accent green is set per component instance, not a style.
- Type: `/Text Styles/` Heading 1, Heading 2, Heading 2 Bold, Heading 3, Heading 4, Body XL, Body L, Body M, Small Mono, Small Mono Footers.
- Layout: Stacks and Grids with the gutter and gap tokens; desktop-first with tablet and phone overrides.
- Code components: `components.json` and the repo's `code/mirror/manifest.json`.

## Maintaining

- Edit `tokens/tokens.json` or `content/**/*.md`, then run `node code/design-system/build.mjs` (regenerates tokens.css, type.css, the site, llms files and components.json). Hand-written: `css/fonts.css`, `css/base.css`, `css/components.css`, `js/components.js`, `site/assets/docs.*`, this file.
- Desktop values come from the Framer project; tablet and phone values are measured on the published site. `qa/home.html` + `qa/compare.js` check Home against the live page at 1200 / 810 / 390.
- When the live site changes, update the affected page in the present tense and add a dated entry to the changelog.
- `code/tokens/micahhoang-tokens.json` (Manrope, `#027aff`) is a retired pre-2026 set. Don't use it.

# Introduction

This is the design system behind micahhoang.com: the foundations every page is built on, the components the site is made of, and the page patterns that put them together. It describes what is live today, measured from the published site, and maps each piece back to its Framer style or code component.

**Foundations** define the tokens for color, type, layout, motion, texture and identity. **Components** go from small pieces like the Mono Label, Tag and Links & Actions up to the Project Card, Index List and Footer. **Patterns** show how the Home, Case Study and Index pages are put together. Each component page has live examples, usage rules, the class API and its Framer mapping.

Pick a page from the sidebar, or press ⌘K to search. Every page also exists as markdown for agents: use the **Markdown** link in its header, or start from [agents.md](../agents.md).

## The system at a glance

```html example
<div class="ds-demo-stack">
  <p class="mh-label">Micah Hoang / Brand designer / Los Angeles, California</p>
  <p class="mh-text-display-xl" style="margin:0">Micah Hoang</p>
  <p class="mh-text-heading" style="margin:0;max-width:11em">Brand designer with a systems mind.</p>
  <hr class="mh-rule">
  <ul class="mh-tags"><li class="mh-tag">Strategy</li><li class="mh-tag">Visual identity</li><li class="mh-tag">Editorial</li></ul>
</div>
```

## Principles

Five words to go back to whenever a decision is unclear: **Considered. Quiet. Alive. Specific. Shipped.** Read [Principles](foundations/principles.md) before designing anything new.

## Start here

- [Colors](foundations/colors.md): two surfaces (Cream and Forest Green) and semantic roles.
- [Typography](foundations/typography.md): GT Standard for display and body, GT Standard Mono for labels.
- [Layout](foundations/layout.md): gutters, grids, breakpoints, rules instead of boxes.
- [Motion](foundations/motion.md): the Snappy ease, flip rails and type reveals.
- [Project Card](components/project-card.md): the main way work appears on the site.
- [Case Study pattern](patterns/case-study.md): the template every project page follows.
- [Changelog](reference/changelog.md): what changed on the site and here, newest first.

<!-- content/foundations/principles.md -->

---
title: Principles
section: Foundations
order: 1
description: Five words that settle design decisions, the voice the site writes in, and the interaction rules behind its behavior.
---

# Principles

The portfolio presents a brand designer who thinks in systems, with range as the proof. Its main reader is a senior brand or design lead with a high craft bar. The site's job is to make the work easy to read without diluting or over-explaining it.

## Five words

| Principle | Means | In practice |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Considered** | Every element earns its place. | No feature because it's cool. If a component isn't on this site, don't add it. |
| **Quiet** | The work is loud enough. The site doesn't need to be. | Cream ground, one green, small mono labels, no decoration. Media carries the color. |
| **Alive** | Small, intentional moments of motion and response. | Flip-rail hovers, type that rises in, a faint moving grain. Never motion for its own sake. |
| **Specific** | "I did X", not "we did Y". Credit is precise. | Meta grids name the client, role and scope. Copy names real outcomes. |
| **Shipped** | Work that exists in the world outweighs work that lives in Figma. | Lead with launched work; show it in context (product, retail, motion). |

What the site is not: an archive (the [Index](../patterns/index-archive.md) holds everything; Home shows six projects), a UX deep-dive site (process lives inside case studies), or a template.

## Voice and copy

- **Plain, first person, present tense.** "I'm a brand designer with a systems mind."
- **Short declaratives.** Case-study intros chain cause and effect: "A photograph becomes a data point. A data point becomes a record."
- **Title Case only for project names**; headings are sentence case ("About Micah").
- **Mono labels are nouns, not sentences**: `/ INDUSTRY`, `VIEW ALL`, `AVAILABLE FOR WORK`.
- **The slash is structural.** Meta labels start with `/ ` and numbered titles read `1 / GAIA`.
- **Credits are exact**: "Client: Self-Initiated Proposal", "Designer: Micah Hoang".
- No exclamation marks, no emoji, no "passionate", "innovative", "pixel-perfect".

## Interaction rules

Apple's interface guidance (WWDC *Designing Fluid Interfaces*, *The Details of UI Typography*, *Principles of Great Design*) applied to this site as a lens, not a redesign. Each rule is labeled:

- **Already true**: the live site behaves this way. Preserve it.
- **New work**: follow it for components that don't exist yet. Don't retrofit live components.
- **Departure**: the brand deliberately does something else. Don't "fix" it.

| Rule | Label | Here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Motion is interruptible, reverses from the current value, and never overshoots | Already true | Flips, media scale and color are CSS transitions on the decelerating Snappy curve. |
| Enter and exit along the same path; anchor overlays to their source | Already true | Flips go up and back down; the lightbox zooms out of the clicked thumbnail; mobile filter panels grow from their trigger; the boot curtain lifts. |
| Exits are faster than entries | Already true | Panels and the lightbox demo open in 250ms and close in 150ms. |
| Reduced motion is gentler, not absent | Already true | Flips run at 0ms, reveals render in place, the grain stops, scroll-to-top jumps. Color and opacity feedback stays. |
| 44px minimum touch targets | Already true | Every mobile link, pill, filter, toggle, menu button and footer row; labels keep their size inside larger hit areas. |
| Show that a row scrolls; use native scrolling | Already true | Mobile pill rows run edge to edge so a cut-off pill signals more; the browser supplies momentum. |
| Direct manipulation: 1:1 tracking, drag threshold, per-axis momentum | Already true | `/play` (see [Motion](motion.md#gesture)). |
| Type: tracking tightens and leading shrinks as size grows; hierarchy from size, not weight | Already true | Display -1% / 100%, body 0 / 140%; bold only on the two display titles. |
| Respond on pointer-down; springs for anything grab-able; rubber-band at edges | New work | Use the `motion.spring.*` tokens. Hover and reveal motion keeps its bezier curves. |
| Text scales with the user's text size | New work | Body-size text should survive 200% browser zoom without overlap. |
| New forms validate inline | New work | Mono labels in `--mh-text-strong`. Don't add a red without asking. |
| Translucent, blurred chrome; scroll-edge fades; depth from shadow | Departure | The brand is flat: opaque surfaces, 1px rules, no shadows. |
| System font | Departure | GT Standard is the brand; `system-ui` is only a fallback. |
| Sound and haptics | Departure | None. |

## Accessibility

- Stroke Gray `#848484` on Cream is **3.43:1**: fine for tags, outlines and secondary meta, below 4.5:1 for small text. Don't use it for anything a visitor must read to use the page; use `--mh-text-body` (Graphite, ~7.2:1) or stronger.
- Forest Green on Cream ≈ 12:1; near-black on Cream ≈ 17:1; Cream on Forest Green ≈ 12:1.
- The nav has no visible current-page state by design; mark the current link with `aria-current="page"`.

## Decision checklist for agents

1. Does an existing component or pattern already cover this? Use it.
2. Does every color, size and duration resolve to a token?
3. Is there one clear display moment per view, with everything else small?
4. Would removing this element lose anything? If not, remove it.
5. Does it work at 390px, with 44px targets and reduced motion?

## Changing the live site

The design system documents micahhoang.com; it doesn't change it. To move a live behavior (for example a touch press state or a current-page nav marker): write it up with the Framer component or style it touches, get Micah's approval, push a dated rollback branch of the affected source (repo `AGENTS.md`), change it in Framer, publish, run published QA (`npm test` for Play files), then update the page here.

<!-- content/foundations/colors.md -->

---
title: Colors
section: Foundations
order: 2
description: Two surfaces, Cream and Forest Green, and the semantic roles that re-map between them.
tokens: [color.primitive.*, color.cream.*, color.green.*]
---

# Colors

## Overview

The palette is deliberately small: a warm Cream ground, one Forest Green for brand and inversion, and a few neutrals for hierarchy. Project media supplies the rest of the color. Always write **semantic roles** (`--mh-text-muted`), never primitives (`--mh-color-light-gray`). Roles re-map automatically inside `data-surface="green"`.

## Primitives

| Token | Value | Framer style | Role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--mh-color-cream` | `#F7F5F0` | `/Colors/Cream` | Page background; text on Forest Green |
| `--mh-color-forest-green` | `#233324` | `/Colors/Forest Green` | Brand: display type, nav, labels; inverse surface |
| `--mh-color-accent-green` | `#25593A` | none: set per instance (`tagHoverColor`, IndexPage hover) | Hover / active for tags, filters, toggles |
| `--mh-color-near-black` | `#141414` | `/Colors/Off-Black` | Rules, index list, lightbox chrome, strong body |
| `--mh-color-graphite` | `#525252` | `/Colors/Text Gray` | Long-form case-study body |
| `--mh-color-light-gray` | `#848484` | `/Colors/Stroke Gray` | Muted text, tags, media stroke |
| `--mh-color-white` | `#FFFFFF` | `/Colors/White` | Lightbox backdrop, media placeholder |
| `--mh-color-white-60` | `#FFFFFF99` | none (published CSS token) | Muted text on Forest Green |
| `--mh-color-grain-umber` | `#501D07` | (GrainOverlay control) | Grain tint only |

### Stroke Gray

Stroke Gray (**`#848484`**, 3.43:1 on Cream) passes 3:1 for large text and UI outlines but not 4.5:1 for small text. Keep it for tags, strokes and secondary meta, never for text someone has to read to use the page. The Home grid (`tagColor`, `strokeColor`) and Index wrapper (`advanced.textTertiary`) store their own copies of this value; change all three together.

## Surfaces

Add `data-surface="cream"` (default) or `data-surface="green"` to any container. It paints `--mh-bg-page` and re-maps every role below for its children.

```html example
<div class="ds-demo-row">
  <div data-surface="cream" style="padding:24px;flex:1">
    <p class="mh-label">Cream surface</p>
    <p class="mh-text-heading" style="margin:16px 0 8px">Brand designer with a systems mind.</p>
    <p class="mh-text-body-sm mh-text-muted" style="margin:0">Muted supporting line.</p>
  </div>
  <div data-surface="green" style="padding:24px;flex:1">
    <p class="mh-label">Green surface</p>
    <p class="mh-text-heading" style="margin:16px 0 8px">Brand designer with a systems mind.</p>
    <p class="mh-text-body-sm mh-text-muted" style="margin:0">Muted supporting line.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Semantic roles

| CSS variable | Cream | Green | Use for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--mh-bg-page` | Cream | Forest Green | Surface background |
| `--mh-bg-media` | White | White | Placeholder behind loading media, lightbox |
| `--mh-bg-hover` | near-black 4% | cream 8% | Row hover wash, code background |
| `--mh-text-brand` | Forest Green | Cream | Display type, nav, labels, section headers |
| `--mh-text-strong` | Near Black | Cream | Lead body, meta values, index rows, H3 |
| `--mh-text-body` | Graphite | White 60% | Long-form paragraphs |
| `--mh-text-muted` | Stroke Gray | White 60% | Headline continuation, tags, tertiary meta |
| `--mh-text-interactive` | Accent Green | White | Hover / active state |
| `--mh-border-rule` | Near Black | Cream | 1px rules and dividers |
| `--mh-border-stroke` | Stroke Gray | White 60% | Tag outlines, media stroke |

## Usage

- **Forest Green is the brand color, not an accent.** It sets display type and labels on Cream and becomes the whole surface for the footer and boot loader.
- **Hierarchy comes from shifting neutrals**: brand → strong → body → muted. Don't add colors to make something stand out; change its size or position.
- **Interactive green appears only on hover/active.** A resting tag is Stroke Gray; it turns Accent Green under the pointer or when selected.
- **Rules are near-black at full opacity**, not a soft gray. The site's crispness depends on this.
- **Media placeholders are white**, so a loading thumbnail reads as a paper card, not a gray hole.

## Don't

- Don't use raw hex values; use roles.
- Don't put Accent Green on large areas or as a button fill.
- Don't introduce a third surface (no gray cards, no dark mode beyond Forest Green).
- Don't use `code/tokens/micahhoang-tokens.json`: its `#027aff` CTA blue and Manrope type are pre-2026 and not on the live site.

<!-- content/foundations/typography.md -->

---
title: Typography
section: Foundations
order: 3
description: GT Standard for display and reading, GT Standard Mono for every label, and a scale with a huge top and a small bottom.
tokens: [font.*, type.*]
---

# Typography

## Overview

Two families do everything. **GT Standard** (L width) sets display type, headings and body. **GT Standard Mono** sets every label, nav item, tag and action, always uppercase at 12–13px. The scale is deliberately polarized: display sizes are huge and tight, everything else is small. There is almost nothing in between.

| Family | CSS variable | Weights | Framer font names |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GT Standard | `--mh-font-sans` | 400, 500, 700 | GT Standard L Regular, GT Standard Trial L Md, GT Standard Trial L Bd |
| GT Standard Mono | `--mh-font-mono` | 400 | GT Standard Mono Regular, GT Standard Mono Trial Rg |

`css/fonts.css` loads the same Framer-hosted files the live site uses and folds them into the families `"MH GT Standard"` and `"MH GT Standard Mono"`, so `font-weight` works normally.

## Scale

Each style is one utility class, `.mh-text-<name>`, generated from `tokens.json`. Sizes are desktop / tablet / mobile.

| Style | Class | Size (D / T / M) | Weight | Leading | Tracking | Framer text style | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Display XL | `mh-text-display-xl` | 120 / 94 / fluid ≤58 | 700 | 100% | -1% | /Heading 1 | Home hero name. Once per site. Phone: `min(58px, (100vw − 40px) / 6.2)`, 56.45px at 390 |
| Display L | `mh-text-display-l` | 70 / 52 / 38 | 700 | 100% | -1% (-2% mobile) | /Heading 2 Bold | Case-study title + muted continuation |
| Display M | `mh-text-display-m` | 70 / 53 / 42 | 400 | 100% | -1% | /Heading 2 | Section headers: "Selected work", "About Micah" |
| Display Footer | `mh-text-display-footer` | 80 / 70 / fluid 28–38 | 400 | 100% | -2% (-1% mobile) | (MagText) | Uppercase footer contact rows; mobile `clamp(27px, (100vw − 40px) / 10, 38px)` |
| Heading | `mh-text-heading` | 35 / 28 / 24 | 400 | 110% | -1% | /Heading 3 | Hero descriptor, case-study section titles |
| Heading S | `mh-text-heading-sm` | 20 | 700 | 140% | 0 | /Heading 4 | Small bold heading |
| Title | `mh-text-title` | 22 | 400 | 120% | 0 | (IndexPage) | Index rows, uppercase |
| Body XL | `mh-text-body-xl` | 22 | 500 | 110% | -1% | /Body XL | Medium-weight lead line |
| Body L | `mh-text-body-lg` | 22 / 18 / 18 | 400 | 120% / 120% / 140% | +1% (0 mobile) | /Body L | Lead paragraphs, About, meta values |
| Body | `mh-text-body` | 18 / 16 / 18 | 400 | 140% | 0 | /Body M | Case-study long-form (580px measure on desktop) |
| Body S | `mh-text-body-sm` | 16 | 400 | 140% | 0 | (none) | Captions, small notes |
| Label | `mh-text-label` / `mh-label` | 13 | 400 mono | 100% | 0 | /Small Mono Footers | Nav, links, ©year, Read more, actions |
| Label relaxed | `mh-text-label-relaxed` / `mh-label[data-leading=relaxed]` | 13 | 400 mono | 130% (140% mobile) | -1% | /Small Mono | GET IN TOUCH, "/ About the project" |
| (Optro) | n/a | 70 | 700 | 100% | -1% | /Optro CRX Heading | Optro CRX case-study hero only; same values as Heading 2 Bold with 0 paragraph spacing |

## Pairings

```html example
<div class="ds-demo-stack">
  <div>
    <p class="mh-label" style="margin-bottom:16px">/ About the project</p>
    <p class="mh-text-body-lg mh-text-strong" style="margin:0;max-width:28em">A photograph becomes a data point. A data point becomes a record. A record becomes a reason to care.</p>
  </div>
  <hr class="mh-rule">
  <div>
    <h3 class="mh-text-heading mh-text-strong" style="margin:0 0 24px">The Insight</h3>
    <p class="mh-text-body mh-text-body mh-measure" style="margin:0">iNaturalist lets people photograph an organism, record where they found it, and share it with a community of naturalists who help identify it.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Source

Framer keeps these in the **`/Text Styles/`** folder (`/Text Styles/Heading 1`, `/Text Styles/Body L`, ...); the table uses the short names. Reading text on a phone is 18px / 140% (Body L and Body M), and every mono label is 13px at every size.

Desktop values come from the Framer project's text styles (read through the Framer MCP). Tablet and mobile values were measured on the published site, because Framer's breakpoint overrides aren't readable through the MCP. `code/tokens/framer-active-text-styles.tokens.json` is an older export: its Heading 1 (110px), Index Title and Paragraph styles no longer match the project.

## Usage

- **One display moment per view.** A page gets one Display XL or Display L; sections get Display M; everything else is Heading or smaller.
- **Display type is tight**: 100% leading and slight negative tracking. Don't loosen it.
- **Mono is always uppercase**, always 12–13px, never for sentences longer than a line.
- **Two-tone headlines.** A case-study title can continue its sentence in `--mh-text-muted` at the same size and weight ("Gaia" + "Turning noticing into a way of caring for the living world.").
- **Body color follows weight of content**: lead copy is `--mh-text-strong`, long-form is `--mh-text-body`.
- **Measure**: long-form body caps at `--mh-measure` (580px).
- **Pretty wrapping**: the live site applies `text-wrap: pretty` to paragraph-size text ≤23px (`ParagraphPrettyWrap`, `EjvkJhv`). Use `text-wrap: balance` for display lines if needed.

## Don't

- Don't use bold (700) below Display L. Weight contrast comes from size.
- Don't set body copy in mono, or labels in sentence case.
- Don't add a third typeface (the old Manrope / Diatype set is retired).
- Don't use letter-spaced uppercase sans as a label substitute; use mono.

<!-- content/foundations/layout.md -->

---
title: Layout
section: Foundations
order: 4
description: Edge-to-edge content inside a 20px gutter, two- and three-column grids, rules instead of boxes, three breakpoints.
tokens: [space.*, layout.*, radius.*, border.*, elevation.*]
---

# Layout

## Overview

Pages run edge to edge inside a small gutter, with no max-width container. Structure comes from a few grids, 1px rules and a lot of vertical space, never from cards or boxes. The system is flat: no shadows, and the only radius is the pill.

## Breakpoints

Desktop-first, matching the Framer frames.

| Name | Range | Framer frame | Media query |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Desktop | ≥ 1200px | 1200 | (default) |
| Tablet | 810–1199px | 810 | `@media (max-width: 1199px)` |
| Mobile | < 810px | 390 | `@media (max-width: 809px)` |

## Gutter and grids

| Token | Desktop | Tablet | Mobile | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--mh-gutter` | 20px | 20px | 20px | Page side padding (`.mh-container`), nav and hero link row |
| `--mh-column-gap` | 20px | 20px | 20px | Card grids, index columns |
| `--mh-split-gap` | 30px | 30px | n/a (stacks) | Two-column text splits (`.mh-split`, meta grid) |
| `--mh-card-row-gap` | 50px | 50px | 50px | Between project-card rows |
| `--mh-measure` | 580px | 580px | 100% | Long-form body |
| `--mh-gutter` | 20px | 20px | 20px | Nav and hero link row; equal to the page gutter |
| `--mh-section-padding-y` | 100px | 100px | 100px | Hero bottom, section bottom |
| `--mh-hero-name-top` | 100px | 100px | 101.4px | Hero top → name line box (nav overlays it); the descriptor follows the name |
| `--mh-section-header-rule-after` | 45px | 45px | 35px | Rule-only section header (Home Selected work) → grid |
| `--mh-section-header-after` | 70px | 70px | 50px | Section title → content |
| `--mh-footer-min-height` | 50vh | 40vh | none | Footer block (content is usually taller) |
| `--mh-touch-target` | n/a | n/a | 44px | Minimum size of every interactive target below 810px |
| `--mh-nav-height` | 53px | 53px | 53px | Sticky nav; grain starts below it |

Grids in use on the live site:

| Grid | Desktop | Tablet | Mobile |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Selected work | 2 columns | 2 columns | 1 column |
| Other projects / index grid | 3 columns | 2 columns | 1 column |
| Case-study meta / split | 2 columns | 2 columns | 1 column |
| Index list | year + 5fr content | year + content | stacked |
| Navigation | 4 zones (name, role, location, links) | 4 zones | name + MENU |

```html example
<div class="mh-split">
  <div style="background:var(--mh-bg-hover);height:120px"></div>
  <div style="background:var(--mh-bg-hover);height:120px"></div>
</div>
```

## Space scale

| Token | Value | Typical use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--mh-space-1` | 4px | Optical nudges |
| `--mh-space-2` | 6px | Tag gap |
| `--mh-space-3` | 8px | Inline groups |
| `--mh-space-4` | 12px | Row padding |
| `--mh-space-5` | 16px | Card internal stack (meta → media → tags) |
| `--mh-space-6` | 20px | Gutter, small blocks |
| `--mh-space-7` | 24px | Small blocks |
| `--mh-space-8` | 30px | Nav link gap, split gap |
| `--mh-space-9` | 40px | Between meta items |
| `--mh-space-10` | 50px | Card row gap |
| `--mh-space-11` | 72px | Inside sections; lightbox padding |
| `--mh-space-12` | 100px | Section padding (Framer) |

## Shape and elevation

| Token | Value | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--mh-radius-none` | 0 | Everything by default: media, sections, surfaces |
| `--mh-radius-hairline` | 2px | Index row hover wash only |
| `--mh-radius-pill` | 250px | Tags, pill actions |
| `--mh-border-hairline` | 1px | The only border width |
| `--mh-elevation-none` | none | The brand is flat |

## Where these numbers come from

Desktop values are read from the Framer project (Home page layers via the Framer MCP): section padding `100px 20px`, rule → title `20px`, title → grid `60px` + `10px` stack gap, grid → View all `30px`, About title → content `30px`, content → Scroll to top `60px`. Tablet and mobile values were measured on micahhoang.com at 810px and 390px, because the MCP can't open breakpoint frames. Re-check them after any Framer layout change.

## Usage

- **Rules, not boxes.** Separate sections with a full-width [Rule](../components/rule.md); separate rows with rules; never wrap content in a bordered or shadowed card.
- **Space is the main tool.** When a layout feels busy, add vertical space between sections before anything else.
- **Align to the gutter.** Every left edge on a page (nav, hero, headings, grid, footer, open menu) sits on `--mh-gutter`, 20px at every breakpoint, so the header doesn't shift between routes. Only full-bleed media and the mobile pill scroll rows cross it.
- **44px targets on touch.** Below 810px every link, pill, filter, toggle and footer row is at least 44×44px. Grow the hit area around the label (padding), not the type.
- **Framer**: build with Stacks (vertical, gap = space token) and Grids (`1fr` columns, gap = column-gap token); set tablet and phone overrides on the breakpoint frames rather than using fixed pixel widths.

## Don't

- Don't cap content with a centered max-width container.
- Don't add drop shadows, rounded media or card backgrounds.
- Don't use borders other than 1px.

<!-- content/foundations/motion.md -->

---
title: Motion
section: Foundations
order: 5
description: Three curves, a short list of durations, the flip rail and type reveal, and how grab-able things move.
tokens: [motion.*]
---

# Motion

## Overview

Motion should feel like the site is alive, not performing. It decelerates into place, moves a few pixels or one line, exits faster than it enters, and respects `prefers-reduced-motion`. Three easing curves cover everything, and the first handles almost all of it.

## Easing

| Token | Curve | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--mh-ease-snappy` | `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` | **Default.** Flips, reveals, hover transforms, media scale, page transitions. |
| `--mh-ease-smooth` | `cubic-bezier(0.12, 0.23, 0.5, 1)` | Symmetric state changes: row hover wash, filter color, panels, count digits, loader bar, the `/play` drawer. |
| `--mh-ease-springy` | `cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1)` | Gesture-like only: rule line draw, cursor trails. Never UI state. |

## Durations

| Token | Value | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--mh-duration-instant` | 150ms | Feedback: row hover wash, count digits, panel and lightbox exit |
| `--mh-duration-fast` | 250ms | Switches: tag color, panel and lightbox entry |
| `--mh-duration-zoom` | 260ms | The live case-study lightbox zoom |
| `--mh-duration-base` | 420ms | **Every text flip** and media hover scale |
| `--mh-duration-reveal` | 900ms | Type reveal; scroll-to-top travel |
| `--mh-duration-page` | 1200ms | Boot curtain lift, page transition |
| `--mh-duration-draw` | 2000ms | Rule line draw (200ms delay) |
| `--mh-stagger-reveal` | 90ms | Between lines in a type reveal |
| `--mh-stagger-media` | 58ms | Between Index thumbnails fading in |

## Flip rail

The site's main hover. A label sits over a second line in a one-line window; on hover or keyboard focus the stack slides up one line. Every flip on the site (nav, social links, View all, Read more, Scroll to top, project titles, Index rows, Play labels) runs **420ms Snappy**. On the live site that timing is one variable, `--mh-flip-duration`, set to `0ms` under reduced motion.

- The second line repeats the label on links and actions. Project cards read **VIEW PROJECT** and Index rows **View Project →**: the hover says what the click does.
- Below 810px nothing rolls; one label stays visible inside a 44px touch target.

```html example
<div class="ds-demo-row">
  <a class="mh-link mh-label" href="#">
    <span class="mh-flip"><span class="mh-flip__track"><span>Work</span><span aria-hidden="true">Work</span></span></span>
  </a>
  <a class="mh-link mh-label" href="#">
    <span class="mh-flip"><span class="mh-flip__track"><span>View all</span><span aria-hidden="true">View all</span></span></span>
  </a>
</div>
```

## Type reveal

Display lines rise into a clipping mask: start at `translateY(115%)`, end at 0, 900ms Snappy, 90ms between lines. Add `.mh-reveal` per line and set `--i` for the order; `components.js` adds `.is-in` when the line enters the viewport. On phones the Home hero renders in place without a reveal.

```html example
<h2 class="mh-text-display-m" style="margin:0">
  <span class="mh-reveal" style="--i:0"><span>About</span></span>
  <span class="mh-reveal" style="--i:1"><span>Micah</span></span>
</h2>
```

## Hover scale

Media inside a link scales to `--mh-scale-hover` (1.02) over 420ms Snappy. The frame doesn't move; only the image does. See [Media Frame](../components/media-frame.md).

## Gesture

Most of the site is hover and scroll. The exception is `/play`, an endless two-axis archive you drag, throw and wheel through. Its physics are the reference for anything new a visitor can grab.

> **`/play` is protected.** Its drag, inertia, video pool and WebKit clamp are performance contracts in the repo `AGENTS.md`. This section describes them; don't retune them. Run `npm test` after changing `Play.tsx` or `ArchivePlayground.tsx`.

| `/play` behavior | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Tap vs drag | 18px of movement before a press becomes a drag (`--mh-gesture-tap-threshold`) |
| Tracking | Pointer capture; the world moves by the pointer delta from where it was grabbed |
| Throw | Per-axis velocity × 1.75, ignored below 220 px/s, clamped at 5200 px/s |
| Deceleration | × 0.85 per 60fps frame (≈0.990/ms); the grid wraps, so there are no edges |
| Edge scroll | Within 90px of an edge, the world drifts at up to 220 px/s |
| Video | The center video pool freezes while moving and refills after it settles; max 6 concurrent in Chromium |
| Drawer | Opens 500ms, closes 400ms, Smooth; keyboard and reduced motion skip it |

Elsewhere, mobile pill rows use native horizontal scrolling, and the case-study carousels use 44px arrows and a scrolling dot strip.

### Springs for new grab-able UI

New things a visitor can drag, swipe or throw use springs, not fixed durations, so they can be caught and reversed mid-flight. Critically damped by default; bounce only after a throw.

| Token | Damping | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `motion.spring.default` | 1.0 | 0.4s |
| `motion.spring.quick` | 1.0 | 0.3s |
| `motion.spring.momentum` | 0.8 | 0.4s (after a flick only) |

```js
// Motion / Framer Motion: bounce = 1 - damping, duration = response
const s = getComputedStyle(document.documentElement)
const spring = (name, velocity = 0) => ({
  type: "spring",
  bounce: 1 - parseFloat(s.getPropertyValue(`--mh-spring-${name}-damping`)),
  duration: parseFloat(s.getPropertyValue(`--mh-spring-${name}-response`)),
  velocity,
})

// Pick the snap target from where a throw would land, then hand off the velocity.
const project = (v, d = 0.99) => (v / 1000) * d / (1 - d)
animate(card, { x: nearestSnap(x + project(v)) }, spring("momentum", v))

// Past a bound, resist progressively instead of stopping.
const rubberband = (over, dim, c = 0.55) => (over * dim * c) / (dim + c * Math.abs(over))
```

Rules: show the pressed state on pointer-down; track 1:1 from the grab offset; wait 18px before committing to a direction; decide open/close by velocity sign; leave along the path you entered; under reduced motion, cross-fade in 200ms instead of moving.

## Don't

- No bounce, elastic or overshoot curves on UI.
- No parallax, scroll-jacking or auto-playing carousels.
- No looping attention animations (the grain shimmer is the only ambient motion).
- Don't build a second page-transition system; `PageTransition` (`gmalnRr`) owns route transitions and the boot curtain.

<!-- content/foundations/texture.md -->

---
title: Texture
section: Foundations
order: 6
description: The umber film grain that sits over every page below the nav, and the one snippet that draws it.
status: live
framer: GrainOverlay (MhR7Ukl)
codeFileId: MhR7Ukl
classes: [mh-grain]
tokens: [texture.grain.*, color.primitive.grain-umber, component.nav.height, z.grain]
---

# Texture

## Overview

A faint, slowly shimmering film grain sits over the page. It warms the Cream ground and keeps large flat areas from looking like a screen: SVG `feTurbulence` noise, desaturated, tinted umber and multiplied at 10%. It starts **below the navigation bar** so the nav stays crisp.

The preview boosts opacity to 0.35 so the grain is visible; the brand value is 0.1.

```html example bleed
<div class="ds-demo-frame" style="height:220px">
  <div style="padding:40px"><p class="mh-text-display-m" style="margin:0">About Micah</p></div>
  <div class="mh-grain" data-contained data-animate style="opacity:.35">
    <svg aria-hidden="true">
      <filter id="mh-grain-demo" x="0" y="0" width="100%" height="100%" color-interpolation-filters="sRGB">
        <feTurbulence type="fractalNoise" baseFrequency="1.14" numOctaves="4" stitchTiles="stitch" seed="7"/>
        <feComponentTransfer>
          <feFuncR type="linear" slope="2.35" intercept="-0.58"/>
          <feFuncG type="linear" slope="2.35" intercept="-0.58"/>
          <feFuncB type="linear" slope="2.35" intercept="-0.58"/>
        </feComponentTransfer>
        <feColorMatrix type="saturate" values="0"/>
        <feColorMatrix type="matrix" values="0.314 0 0 0 0  0.114 0 0 0 0  0.027 0 0 0 0  0 0 0 0 1"/>
      </filter>
      <rect width="100%" height="100%" filter="url(#mh-grain-demo)"/>
    </svg>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Page snippet

Once per page, as the last child of `body`. The last matrix multiplies the gray noise by umber `#501D07` (80/255, 29/255, 7/255).

```html
<div class="mh-grain" data-animate aria-hidden="true">
  <svg><filter id="mh-grain" x="0" y="0" width="100%" height="100%" color-interpolation-filters="sRGB">
    <feTurbulence type="fractalNoise" baseFrequency="1.14" numOctaves="4" stitchTiles="stitch" seed="7"/>
    <feComponentTransfer><feFuncR type="linear" slope="2.35" intercept="-0.58"/><feFuncG type="linear" slope="2.35" intercept="-0.58"/><feFuncB type="linear" slope="2.35" intercept="-0.58"/></feComponentTransfer>
    <feColorMatrix type="saturate" values="0"/>
    <feColorMatrix type="matrix" values="0.314 0 0 0 0  0.114 0 0 0 0  0.027 0 0 0 0  0 0 0 0 1"/>
  </filter><rect width="100%" height="100%" filter="url(#mh-grain)"/></svg>
</div>
```

## Values

| Token | Value | Framer control |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--mh-grain-opacity` | 0.1 | Grain Opacity |
| `--mh-grain-blend` | multiply | Blend |
| `--mh-grain-color` | `#501D07` | Color |
| `--mh-grain-base-frequency` | 1.14 | Grain Size |
| `--mh-grain-octaves` | 4 | Detail |
| `--mh-grain-exposure` / `-contrast` | -0.58 / 2.35 | Exposure / Contrast |
| `--mh-grain-shimmer-fps` | 16 | Shimmer FPS |

| Attribute | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `class="mh-grain"` | Fixed layer below the nav: opacity 0.1, multiply, `pointer-events: none` |
| `data-contained` | Absolute inside a positioned parent (previews) |
| `data-animate` | Re-seeds the noise 16 times a second; stops under reduced motion |

## Framer mapping

`GrainOverlay` (`MhR7Ukl`) portals a fixed layer to `<body>` with **Clear Nav** on, so the grain starts at the nav's bottom edge (full height during page transitions, so no blank strip shows). On `/play` it's static outside WebKit and turned off on WebKit (`disableOnWebKit`), a Play performance contract; keep it that way.

## Don't

- Don't raise opacity above 0.1 or switch the blend away from multiply; it reads as dirt.
- Don't put grain inside components or on media; it's one page-level layer.
- Don't add other textures (paper, noise PNGs, gradients).

# Identity

## Overview

The identity is the name. Two drawn marks exist, both outlined from the personal-identity Figma file: the compact **©MH monogram**, which the boot loader shows, and the full **© Micah Hoang wordmark**. Everywhere else the name is set in type. Consistency is what makes it work: the same words, set the same way, in the same places.

## Monogram

```html example surface=green
<img class="mh-monogram" src="../../assets/identity/monogram-cream.svg" alt="©MH">
```

```html example
<img class="mh-monogram" src="../../assets/identity/monogram-forest-green.svg" alt="©MH" style="--mh-monogram-size: 120px">
```

| File | Fill | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `assets/identity/monogram.svg` | `currentColor` | Inline, takes the text color |
| `assets/identity/monogram-cream.svg` | Cream | `<img>` on Forest Green |
| `assets/identity/monogram-forest-green.svg` | Forest Green | `<img>` on Cream |

- **Source:** Figma personal-identity node `168:541`, saved unchanged at `assets/identity/micah-hoang-monogram.svg`. The design-system copies use the cleaned version (`micah-hoang-monogram-clean.svg`): three direct paths, with the © drawn as its filled outline plus a 4.94-unit centered stroke instead of the export's masked strokes. No masks, images or `use` elements.
- **Where:** the boot loader, at 237.5px desktop and 190px tablet (`--mh-monogram-width`).
- **Proportions:** viewBox `629.319 × 208.043` (about 3 : 1). Set width only.
- **Color:** Cream on Forest Green or Forest Green on Cream.

## Wordmark

```html example surface=green
<img class="mh-wordmark" src="../../assets/identity/wordmark-cream.svg" alt="© Micah Hoang">
```

```html example
<img class="mh-wordmark" src="../../assets/identity/wordmark-forest-green.svg" alt="© Micah Hoang" style="--mh-wordmark-width: 278px">
```

| File | Fill | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `assets/identity/wordmark.svg` | `currentColor` | Inline in HTML or a code component, so it takes the text color |
| `assets/identity/wordmark-cream.svg` | Cream `#F7F5F0` | `<img>` on Forest Green |
| `assets/identity/wordmark-forest-green.svg` | Forest Green `#233324` | `<img>` on Cream |

- **Source:** Figma personal-identity node `91:521`, saved in the repo at `assets/identity/micah-hoang-copyright.svg`. The design-system copies use the live loader's corrected outline: the © is one filled and stroked path (no mask), which removes the antialiasing seams the original export showed. 11 paths, no bitmaps.
- **Proportions:** viewBox `7682.3 × 1025.01` (about 7.5 : 1). Never stretch it; set width only.
- **Size:** never wider than the viewport minus 64px (`.mh-wordmark` defaults to 556 / 444px, its old loader size). Don't render it below about 200px wide.
- **Status:** not placed on the live site; use it where the full name has to stand alone as a mark.
- **Color:** Cream on Forest Green or Forest Green on Cream. No other colors, outlines or effects.
- **Render as vector.** Inline SVG or `<img>`. The live loader moved off a CSS mask because it looked soft at small sizes.

## Marks set in type

| Mark | Setting | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Micah Hoang** (display) | Display XL, GT Standard Bold, Forest Green | Home hero, once |
| **MICAH HOANG** (label) | Mono label, uppercase | Nav, top left, every page; links home |
| **©2026** | Mono label | Right end of the hero link row and the footer bar |
| **MICAH.HOANG @HEY.COM** | Display Footer + mono superscript | Footer contact |

```html example
<div class="ds-demo-stack">
  <p class="mh-text-display-xl" style="margin:0">Micah Hoang</p>
  <div class="ds-demo-row" style="justify-content:space-between">
    <span class="mh-label">Micah Hoang</span>
    <span class="mh-label">Brand designer</span>
    <span class="mh-label">©2026</span>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Descriptor

The positioning line sits under the hero name in the Heading style, broken over two lines:

> Brand designer with
> a systems mind.

The nav repeats it in short form: `BRAND DESIGNER` and `LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA`.

## Usage

- Write the name exactly "Micah Hoang"; uppercase only through mono labels.
- The copyright year comes from `FooterCopyrightYear` (`BF2H03E`) in Framer; don't hard-code a different year. The wordmark's © carries no year.
- Use the drawn marks only where the name stands alone. Don't put them in the nav, footer or hero, which set the name in type.
- Don't draw new marks (another monogram, a favicon glyph, a logo). The ©MH monogram and the wordmark are the complete set.

<!-- content/components/label.md -->

---
title: Mono Label
section: Components
order: 1
description: The uppercase 13px mono line that carries every piece of metadata, navigation and UI text on the site.
status: live
framer: Text styles /Text Styles/Small Mono Footers and /Text Styles/Small Mono
classes: [mh-label]
tokens: [type.label, color.*.text.brand, color.*.text.muted]
---

# Mono Label

## Examples

```html example
<div class="ds-demo-stack">
  <p class="mh-label">Los Angeles, California</p>
  <p class="mh-label" data-tone="muted">2D motion</p>
  <p class="mh-label" data-leading="relaxed">/ About the project</p>
</div>
```

```html example surface=green
<p class="mh-label">Get in touch</p>
```

## Usage

The Mono Label is the site's second voice. Display type makes the statement; labels carry everything else: nav, meta, eyebrows, counts, years, actions.

- **Always uppercase.** The class sets `text-transform`, so write the source in natural case ("Los Angeles, California") and let CSS uppercase it. Screen readers then read words, not letters.
- **One line.** If it wraps into a sentence, it should be body text.
- **The slash is a structural mark.** Meta headings start with `/ ` (`/ Scope`), and numbered titles read `1 / Gaia`.
- **Tone follows role.** Brand (default) for nav and headings, `muted` for tertiary meta, `strong` for list data.

## API

| Attribute | Values | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `class="mh-label"` | n/a | 13px GT Standard Mono, 100% leading, uppercase |
| `data-tone` | `muted`, `strong` | `--mh-text-muted` / `--mh-text-strong` |
| `data-leading` | `relaxed` | 130% leading, -1% tracking (Small Mono) for labels stacked over values |

Or use the plain utility `mh-text-label` on any element.

## Accessibility

- Use real elements: `<p>` for standalone labels, `<dt>` in meta lists, `<span>` inline.
- Don't type the text in capitals; let CSS do it.

## Framer mapping

- Text styles: **Small Mono Footers** (13px, 100%, 0 tracking) for nav, links and meta; **Small Mono** (13px, 130%, -1%) for labels stacked over content (`data-leading="relaxed"`).
- Font: GT Standard Mono Regular (falls back to GT Standard Mono Trial Rg).

## Don't

- Don't use mono for paragraphs or headings.
- Don't letter-space it; tracking is 0.
- Don't bold it.

<!-- content/components/links-actions.md -->

---
title: Links & Actions
section: Components
order: 2
description: Every clickable piece of text. Mono links and actions with the flip rail, link lists, inline links, outlined pills and Scroll to top. There is no filled button.
status: live
framer: Native Text Link (dVTZgYLeH); Text Flip Up (TextEncryptionEffect, p7tSTaD); ScrollToTopButton (gh4ngZN)
codeFileId: p7tSTaD
classes: [mh-link, mh-flip, mh-flip__track, mh-link-list, mh-action, mh-scroll-top]
tokens: [type.label, motion.duration.base, motion.ease.snappy, motion.distance.flip-gap, component.link-list.gap, layout.touch-target]
---

# Links & Actions

## Examples

### Flip links: nav, social, actions

```html example
<div class="ds-demo-stack">
  <div class="ds-demo-row">
    <a class="mh-link mh-label" href="#"><span class="mh-flip"><span class="mh-flip__track"><span>Work</span><span aria-hidden="true">Work</span></span></span></a>
    <a class="mh-link mh-label" href="#"><span class="mh-flip"><span class="mh-flip__track"><span>Play</span><span aria-hidden="true">Play</span></span></span></a>
    <a class="mh-link mh-label" href="#"><span class="mh-flip"><span class="mh-flip__track"><span>Index</span><span aria-hidden="true">Index</span></span></span></a>
    <a class="mh-link mh-label" href="#"><span class="mh-flip"><span class="mh-flip__track"><span>About</span><span aria-hidden="true">About</span></span></span></a>
  </div>
  <ul class="mh-link-list mh-label">
    <li><a class="mh-link" href="#"><span class="mh-flip"><span class="mh-flip__track"><span>LinkedIn</span><span aria-hidden="true">LinkedIn</span></span></span></a></li>
    <li><a class="mh-link" href="#"><span class="mh-flip"><span class="mh-flip__track"><span>Resume</span><span aria-hidden="true">Resume</span></span></span></a></li>
    <li><a class="mh-link" href="#"><span class="mh-flip"><span class="mh-flip__track"><span>Email</span><span aria-hidden="true">Email</span></span></span></a></li>
    <li><a class="mh-link" href="#"><span class="mh-flip"><span class="mh-flip__track"><span>Cosmos</span><span aria-hidden="true">Cosmos</span></span></span></a></li>
  </ul>
  <div class="ds-demo-row">
    <a class="mh-action" href="#"><span class="mh-flip"><span class="mh-flip__track"><span>View all</span><span aria-hidden="true">View all</span></span></span></a>
    <a class="mh-action" href="#"><span class="mh-flip"><span class="mh-flip__track"><span>Read more</span><span aria-hidden="true">Read more</span></span></span></a>
    <button class="mh-action mh-scroll-top" type="button"><span class="mh-flip"><span class="mh-flip__track"><span>Scroll to top</span><span aria-hidden="true">Scroll to top</span></span></span></button>
  </div>
</div>
```

### Pill and inline link

```html example
<div class="ds-demo-stack">
  <div class="ds-demo-row">
    <a class="mh-action" data-variant="pill" href="#">Resume ↗</a>
    <button class="mh-action" data-variant="pill" type="button" disabled>Unavailable</button>
  </div>
  <p class="mh-text-body-lg mh-text-strong" style="margin:0;max-width:30em">I'm a brand designer with a systems mind. Read the <a class="mh-link" data-variant="inline" href="#">full story</a>.</p>
</div>
```

## Usage

| Kind | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| Flip link (`mh-link` + `mh-flip`) | Nav, social links (LinkedIn, Resume, Email, Cosmos, GitHub) |
| Link list (`mh-link-list`) | Comma-joined social links in the hero and footer bar, 10px apart |
| Text action (`mh-action`) | View all, Read more, Scroll to top, Clear filters |
| Pill (`mh-action data-variant="pill"`) | A standalone action that needs a visible boundary. At most one per view |
| Inline link (`data-variant="inline"`) | Links inside body copy: 1px underline, green on hover |

- **One flip everywhere:** 420ms Snappy, one line up, on hover and keyboard focus. The second line repeats the label; only project cards and Index rows say what the click does (VIEW PROJECT, View Project →). Don't invent other hover copy.
- **No filled button**, no shadows, no rounded rectangles. Direction is typed into the label (↗ external, ↑ top, → next), never an icon.
- **Scroll to top** sits on the left gutter 60px below the last content on long pages (Home, About) and glides to the top in 900ms; under reduced motion it jumps.
- **Mobile (below 810px):** nothing rolls. One label stays visible in its 13px mask and the link grows to a 44px touch target (15.5px above and below), centered on the label so surrounding spacing doesn't move.

## API

| Class / attribute | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `mh-link` | Resets link color and underline; inherits text |
| `mh-flip` › `mh-flip__track` › two `span`s | One-line window that slides up on hover/focus of the parent `a`/`button`. `--mh-flip-h` sets the window (default `1em`) |
| `mh-link-list` | Horizontal list; commas added by CSS |
| `mh-action` | Mono label, uppercase, no chrome |
| `data-variant="pill"` | 1px currentColor outline, pill radius, 24px min height, green on hover |
| `data-variant="inline"` | On `mh-link`: 1px underline at 0.18em |
| `mh-scroll-top` | On an `mh-action`; `components.js` scrolls the document (or `data-target`) to the top |
| `disabled` / `aria-disabled="true"` | 40% opacity, no pointer events |

## Accessibility

- The second span is `aria-hidden="true"`, so the label is read once.
- Focus shows the flip plus a 1px outline at 3px offset.
- Use `<a>` to navigate and `<button type="button">` for in-page actions; icon-only controls (lightbox ← → ×) need `aria-label`.

## Framer mapping

- **Native Text Link** (`dVTZgYLeH`): nav, View all and Read more. Its Link variable sits on the outer frame only (no nested links).
- **Text Flip Up** (`TextEncryptionEffect.tsx`, `p7tSTaD`): the hero and footer-bar social labels. It replaced the old letter scramble with a line-height-aware flip.
- **ScrollToTopButton** (`gh4ngZN`): label `scroll to top`, 900ms scroll, hands off to the global Lenis instance.
- The shared timing comes from `ResumeAssetHost` (`xDqfenf`): `--mh-flip-duration: 420ms` and `--mh-flip-ease`, with `0ms` under reduced motion. Code components read the same variable.
- `CaseStudyScrambleText` (`dHFQCIH`) is a plain hover-color link despite its name.

<!-- content/components/tag.md -->

---
title: Tag
section: Components
order: 4
description: Outlined mono pills that name a project's disciplines and double as filters.
status: live
framer: Rendered by HomeSelectedWorkGrid (FecepLS) and IndexPage (rgAZFOv) from CMS discipline fields
codeFileId: FecepLS
classes: [mh-tags, mh-tag]
tokens: [type.label, radius.pill, color.*.border.stroke, color.*.text.muted, color.*.text.interactive, motion.duration.fast, component.tag.*]
---

# Tag

## Examples

```html example
<ul class="mh-tags">
  <li class="mh-tag">Strategy</li>
  <li class="mh-tag">Visual identity</li>
  <li class="mh-tag">Editorial</li>
</ul>
```

### Interactive (links or filter toggles)

```html example
<div class="mh-tags">
  <a class="mh-tag" href="#">2D motion</a>
  <a class="mh-tag" href="#">3D motion</a>
  <button class="mh-tag" type="button" aria-pressed="true">Social media</button>
  <button class="mh-tag" type="button" aria-pressed="false">Packaging</button>
</div>
```

```html example surface=green
<ul class="mh-tags"><li class="mh-tag">Product</li><li class="mh-tag">Packaging</li></ul>
```

## Usage

- Tags list a project's **disciplines** (Strategy, Visual identity, UX/UI, 2D motion, Packaging...). Industry goes in the index row, not a tag.
- Up to three per card, in CMS order.
- At rest a tag is Stroke Gray text with a Stroke Gray outline. Interactive tags (links or toggle buttons) turn Accent Green on hover; a pressed toggle stays green.
- On the live site, clicking a grid tag on `/index` toggles that discipline filter in place.

## Responsive

| Breakpoint | Type | Box | Row |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Desktop | 13px, 100% leading | 24px min height, padding `5px 10px 6px` (26px tall) | Wraps, 6px gap |
| Tablet | 13px, 100% leading | 23px min height, padding `5px 9px 6px` (26px tall) | Wraps, 5px gap |
| Mobile | 13px, 1.3 leading | 44px touch target, padding `8px 24px 7px` | One line, scrolls sideways, 5px gap |

On mobile the row runs from screen edge to screen edge while its first pill rests on the 20px gutter, so pills further along are visibly cut off at the edge, which signals that the row scrolls. Scrolling is the browser's own (momentum and interruption for free); the scrollbar is hidden and there are no fade gradients. The 8 / 7px vertical padding lifts the mono capitals half a pixel to sit optically centered. A 4px clearance above and below keeps borders and focus rings from clipping.

## API

| Class / attribute | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `mh-tags` | Wrapping flex row, 6px gap (5px below 1200px); on mobile a single row that scrolls sideways edge to edge; use on `ul` or `div` |
| `mh-tag` | 13px mono pill, 24px min height, `5px 10px 6px` padding |
| `a.mh-tag` / `button.mh-tag` | Hover → `--mh-text-interactive`, 250ms Snappy |
| `aria-pressed="true"` | Selected state (green), for filter toggles |

## Accessibility

- Static tags: `li` elements in a `ul`.
- Filter tags: `<button type="button" aria-pressed>`; `components.js` toggles the state.
- Long labels truncate with an ellipsis; keep labels to two words.

## Framer mapping

- Home cards: `HomeSelectedWorkGrid` (`FecepLS`). Tag color comes from a property control (default `#25593a` for hover); Show Tags toggle.
- `/index` grid: `IndexPage` (`rgAZFOv`) via `IndexPageGridPreview` (`LgIzFjJ`). Tags are `<button>`s that toggle disciplines through `IndexFilterContext`.
- Values come from CMS `All Projects` (`yTHrQWMIY`) category fields; never hard-code tag lists.

## Don't

- Don't fill tags with color or use them as status badges.
- Don't mix tag sizes in one row.
- Don't use tags as primary navigation.

---
title: Rule
section: Components
order: 5
description: The 1px near-black line that does the work boxes and cards do elsewhere, with an optional draw-in.
status: live
framer: 1px Frame (fill /Near Black) or native "Line Animation"; LineAnimationBorder (j7WYIMf)
codeFileId: j7WYIMf
classes: [mh-rule]
tokens: [border.hairline, color.*.border.rule, motion.duration.draw, motion.ease.springy]
---

# Rule

## Examples

```html example
<div class="ds-demo-stack">
  <hr class="mh-rule">
  <div class="ds-demo-row" style="justify-content:space-between">
    <span class="mh-label">LinkedIn, Resume, Email, Cosmos</span>
    <span class="mh-label">©2026</span>
  </div>
  <hr class="mh-rule">
</div>
```

### Line draw

Scroll it into view (or reload) to see it draw from the left.

```html example
<hr class="mh-rule" data-draw>
```

## Usage

- A full-width rule separates **sections** (above a Section Header), **groups** (index year groups) and **rows** (index rows).
- Rules are always 1px, full opacity, `--mh-border-rule`. On Forest Green they turn Cream.
- Rules span the content width (gutter to gutter), never a fraction of it.
- Line draw is for the first appearance of a major rule (hero base, section starts). Don't animate row dividers.

## API

| Attribute | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `<hr class="mh-rule">` | 1px full-width rule |
| `data-draw` | Starts at `scaleX(0)`; draws over 2000ms Springy with a 200ms delay once `components.js` adds `.is-in` |

## Accessibility

- Use `<hr>` when the rule marks a thematic break; use a CSS border (`border-top: var(--mh-border-hairline) solid var(--mh-border-rule)`) when it's purely visual, as in index rows.

## Framer mapping

- Static: a 1px-tall Frame filled with near-black `#141414`.
- Animated: native **Line Animation** (0.2s delay, 2s, `[0.25, 1, 0.5, 1]`) or `LineAnimationBorder` (`j7WYIMf`) for a non-destructive border frame with a `Viewport Once` trigger.
- Index dividers are controlled by `IndexPage` (`rgAZFOv`) `dividerSubtle` and stay full-opacity `#141414`.

## Don't

- Don't use gray or semi-transparent rules.
- Don't use 2px or dashed rules.
- Don't box content with four rules; a rule only ever runs horizontally.

# Section Header

## Examples

```html example
<header class="mh-section-header">
  <hr class="mh-rule">
  <h2 class="mh-section-header__title">Other projects</h2>
</header>
```

### With an action

```html example
<header class="mh-section-header">
  <hr class="mh-rule">
  <h2 class="mh-section-header__title">Other projects</h2>
  <a class="mh-action" href="#"><span class="mh-flip"><span class="mh-flip__track"><span>View all</span><span aria-hidden="true">View all</span></span></span></a>
</header>
```

### With reveal

```html example
<header class="mh-section-header">
  <hr class="mh-rule" data-draw>
  <h2 class="mh-section-header__title">
    <span class="mh-reveal" style="--i:0"><span>About Micah</span></span>
  </h2>
</header>
```

### Rule only

```html example
<header class="mh-section-header" data-variant="rule">
  <hr class="mh-rule">
</header>
<ul class="mh-project-grid">
  <li class="mh-project-card"><a class="mh-project-card__link" href="#"><div class="mh-project-card__meta mh-label"><span>1</span><span>/</span><span class="mh-flip"><span class="mh-flip__track"><span>Gaia</span><span aria-hidden="true">View project</span></span></span></div><div class="mh-media"><img src="../../assets/samples/gaia.jpg" alt=""></div></a></li>
  <li class="mh-project-card"><a class="mh-project-card__link" href="#"><div class="mh-project-card__meta mh-label"><span>2</span><span>/</span><span class="mh-flip"><span class="mh-flip__track"><span>AirPods Pro 3</span><span aria-hidden="true">View project</span></span></span></div><div class="mh-media" data-stroke><img src="../../assets/samples/airpods.jpg" alt=""></div></a></li>
</ul>
```

## Usage

- Use for top-level page sections: About Micah, Other projects, Index.
- **Rule only** (`data-variant="rule"`): Home's Selected work has no title, because the six numbered cards already say what they are. The rule sits 6px into the section (1px on phone) and the grid starts 45px below it (35px on phone).
- Titles are sentence case, two or three words. They label the section; they aren't headlines.
- Spacing (Framer): the previous section ends with 100px bottom padding; rule → title 20px; title → content 70px (50px mobile) via the header's own bottom padding. Use `data-spacing="compact"` for About (30px, 20px mobile).
- Multi-word titles reveal word by word: wrap each word in a `span`; words sit 15px apart (8px mobile).
- An optional action (View all) sits on the title's baseline at the right edge.

## API

| Class | Element | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mh-section-header` | `header` | Grid: title left, optional action right |
| `mh-rule` | `hr` | First child; spans both columns |
| `mh-section-header__title` | `h2` | Display M (70 / 53 / 42px, regular, Forest Green); word spans 15px apart |
| `data-variant="rule"` | `header` | Rule only, no title; 45px (35px phone) to the content |
| `data-spacing="compact"` | `header` | 30px (20px mobile) below instead of 70px |

## Framer mapping

- Text style **Heading 2** (GT Standard L Regular). The live site renders the title at 70px with -1% tracking.
- The rule is a 1px frame or Line Animation above the title in a vertical Stack; the title row has 20px top padding.
- The reveal is Framer's native Appear effect, normalized by `PageTransition` (`gmalnRr`) to 900ms / 90ms stagger / Snappy / 115% start.

## Don't

- Don't use bold for section titles; bold is reserved for the hero and case-study titles.
- Don't add eyebrows or numbers ("01 / Work") above section titles.

# Navigation

## Examples

```html example bleed
<nav class="mh-nav" aria-label="Primary" style="position:relative">
  <a class="mh-nav__name mh-link mh-label" href="#">
    <span class="mh-flip"><span class="mh-flip__track"><span>Micah Hoang</span><span aria-hidden="true">Micah Hoang</span></span></span>
  </a>
  <p class="mh-nav__role mh-label">Brand designer</p>
  <p class="mh-nav__location mh-label">Los Angeles, California</p>
  <ul class="mh-nav__links mh-label">
    <li><a class="mh-link" href="#" aria-current="page"><span class="mh-flip"><span class="mh-flip__track"><span>Work</span><span aria-hidden="true">Work</span></span></span></a></li>
    <li><a class="mh-link" href="#"><span class="mh-flip"><span class="mh-flip__track"><span>Play</span><span aria-hidden="true">Play</span></span></span></a></li>
    <li><a class="mh-link" href="#"><span class="mh-flip"><span class="mh-flip__track"><span>Index</span><span aria-hidden="true">Index</span></span></span></a></li>
    <li><a class="mh-link" href="#"><span class="mh-flip"><span class="mh-flip__track"><span>About</span><span aria-hidden="true">About</span></span></span></a></li>
  </ul>
  <button class="mh-nav__menu mh-label" type="button" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="mh-menu-demo">Menu</button>
</nav>
<div class="mh-nav-panel" id="mh-menu-demo" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-label="Menu" data-surface="green" hidden>
  <div class="mh-nav-panel__header">
    <a class="mh-link mh-label" href="#">Micah Hoang</a>
    <button class="mh-nav__menu mh-label" type="button" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="mh-menu-demo">Close</button>
  </div>
  <ul class="mh-nav-panel__routes">
    <li><a href="#" aria-current="page">Work</a></li>
    <li><a href="#">Play</a></li>
    <li><a href="#">Index</a></li>
    <li><a href="#">About</a></li>
  </ul>
  <ul class="mh-nav-panel__social mh-label">
    <li><a href="#">LinkedIn</a></li>
    <li><a href="#">Email</a></li>
    <li><a href="#">GitHub</a></li>
  </ul>
</div>
```

Resize below 810px to see the MENU button; it opens the full-screen panel.

## Anatomy

| Zone | Content | Below 810px |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Name | "Micah Hoang", links to `/` | Kept |
| Role | "Brand designer" | Hidden |
| Location | "Los Angeles, California" | Hidden |
| Links | Work, Play, Index, About | Replaced by MENU; routes appear in the full-screen panel |

Desktop columns are fixed: name 258px, role 340px, location fills, links hug the right edge (measured identical at 1200 and 1280). Tablet uses fixed 123px / 145px columns. Links sit 31px apart. The nav gutter is 20px at every breakpoint.

## Usage

- Same bar, same copy, on every page. Only the links change state.
- Routes: Work → `/`, Play → `/play`, Index → `/index`, About → `/about`.
- The bar is 53px tall with 20px side gutters. Desktop hides on scroll down and returns on scroll up. Below 810px it stays fixed and visible.
- Grain starts below the nav, so the bar always stays crisp.
- The live site doesn't style the current link. Mark it with `aria-current="page"` for assistive tech only.

### Mobile menu

- The **Hybrid** and **Black** layout templates mount the native **Mobile Navigation** component (`qajbM_0Ju`) on Phone only. Desktop and tablet retain their existing header.
- Edit **Assets → Mobile Navigation → Closed / Open** for the layout, labels, links, and colors. The component owns its native Click interactions with an Instant transition.
- MENU and CLOSE each use one text node inside a 13px-high `Label Mask` with hidden overflow, inside a 60×44 hit area. There is no rollover duplicate and no runtime-generated replacement label.
- `NavigationScrollGuard` adds dialog semantics, keyboard controls, focus containment, background inertness, and viewport-height handling to the native component. It does not create or own the menu's visual content.
- The open panel uses Forest Green with Cream type, the existing responsive **Heading 2** text style (GT Standard, 42px on phone; `type.display-m`), 13px GT Standard Mono labels, and the existing 20px nav gutters.
- Route labels use title case: Work, Play, Index, About. Each retains the shared Heading 2 style; do not introduce a separate menu text style or uppercase the route copy. LinkedIn, Email, and GitHub sit at the bottom. CLOSE occupies the same 60×44 box as MENU; route rows fit their text line height plus 12px top and bottom padding (`--mh-space-4`). This gives 66px rows with 42px phone type and prevents larger canvas type from overlapping.
- The open variant contains keyboard focus, supports Enter/Space and Escape, locks background scrolling, and restores focus and scroll on close. It closes and cleans up when resizing to 810px or wider.
- Mobile header links use ordinary browser navigation without the desktop curtain interception. Selecting Work while already on Home closes the menu and returns to the top.
- Mobile Home name, descriptor, and Selected/work headings render in place. Their previous appear/replay effects visibly restarted after settling. Desktop motion is unchanged.

## API

| Class | Element | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mh-nav` | `nav` | Sticky; grid `258px 340px 1fr auto` (tablet `123px 145px 1fr auto`), 53px tall |
| `mh-nav__name` | `a` | Flip link |
| `mh-nav__role`, `mh-nav__location` | `p` | Static labels, hidden on mobile |
| `mh-nav__links` | `ul` | Flip links, 31px gap; hidden below 810px |
| `mh-nav__menu` | `button[aria-controls][aria-expanded]` | Mobile only: MENU / CLOSE, 60×44px target, label right-aligned to the gutter |
| `mh-nav-panel` | `div[role=dialog][hidden]` | Mobile only: full-screen Forest Green panel (`data-surface="green"`) |
| `mh-nav-panel__routes` | `ul` | Display M (42px) routes in title case, 12px above and below: 66px rows |
| `mh-nav-panel__social` | `ul.mh-label` | LinkedIn, Email, GitHub at the bottom; 44×44px targets |

`components.js` opens and closes the panel, locks page scroll, restores focus to MENU, closes on Escape, and closes when the viewport grows past 810px.

## Accessibility

- `<nav aria-label="Primary">`, links in a list.
- Add a "Skip to content" link before the nav in real pages.
- Keep visible focus on every link (the flip triggers on focus too).

## Framer mapping

- The live bars are native layers in **Hybrid** and **Black** layout templates. Desktop links use the shared **Text Link** hover variants.
- Mobile Navigation asset: `qajbM_0Ju`; Closed `wAv2cBhhn`; Open `gdGCs2vyp`. The Phone instances are `tK8RS0JyeF6qyNICpc` (Hybrid) and `rzjQrYrtJwE5QaaCdz` (Black). Their desktop source instances remain hidden.
- [Open Mobile Navigation in Framer](https://framer.com/projects/Micah-Hoang-Portfolio--BvGjN2gCRDHG41LzAVYE-b78r3?node=qajbM_0Ju).
- Rollover labels: both stacked copies use 100% line height (13px), so the replacement lands exactly on the resting label's 20px top.
- Scroll behavior and global smooth scroll: `NavigationScrollGuard` (`Wnd19lx`), mounted through `ResumeAssetHost` (`xDqfenf`). It owns the single Lenis 1.3.26 instance (`lerp 0.12`, native touch) and is destroyed on `/play`.
- Exposed controls: `Smooth`, `Scroll feel`.

## Don't

- Don't add a logo, hamburger icon or CTA button to the bar.
- Don't add a new palette or decorative blur. The mobile panel uses the existing Forest Green/Cream surface pairing.
- Don't change the order of the four zones.

# Footer

## Examples

```html example bleed surface=green
<footer class="mh-footer" data-surface="green">
  <p class="mh-label mh-footer__eyebrow">Get in touch</p>
  <ul class="mh-footer__contacts">
    <li><a class="mh-footer__contact" href="#">micah.hoang<sup>@hey.com</sup></a></li>
    <li><a class="mh-footer__contact" href="#">LinkedIn<sup>Connect</sup></a></li>
    <li><a class="mh-footer__contact" href="#">Cosmos<sup>Inspire</sup></a></li>
    <li><a class="mh-footer__contact" href="#">GitHub<sup>Build</sup></a></li>
  </ul>
  <div class="mh-footer__bar">
    <p class="mh-label">Available for work</p>
    <ul class="mh-link-list mh-label">
      <li><a class="mh-link" href="#"><span class="mh-flip"><span class="mh-flip__track"><span>LinkedIn</span><span aria-hidden="true">LinkedIn</span></span></span></a></li>
      <li><a class="mh-link" href="#"><span class="mh-flip"><span class="mh-flip__track"><span>Resume</span><span aria-hidden="true">Resume</span></span></span></a></li>
      <li><a class="mh-link" href="#"><span class="mh-flip"><span class="mh-flip__track"><span>Cosmos</span><span aria-hidden="true">Cosmos</span></span></span></a></li>
      <li><a class="mh-link" href="#"><span class="mh-flip"><span class="mh-flip__track"><span>GitHub</span><span aria-hidden="true">GitHub</span></span></span></a></li>
    </ul>
    <p class="mh-label">©2026</p>
  </div>
</footer>
```

## Anatomy

1. **Eyebrow** (`mh-footer__eyebrow`): "Get in touch", `/Small Mono` (130% leading at every size), 20px from the top.
2. **Contacts**: four Display Footer rows, uppercase, each with a `/Small Mono Footers` superscript 10px to its right: `MICAH.HOANG` `@HEY.COM`, `LINKEDIN` `CONNECT`, `COSMOS` `INSPIRE`, `GITHUB` `BUILD` (added 2026-10).
   - Desktop / tablet: 80 / 70px, -2% tracking, rows 12px apart, superscript 2px down.
   - Mobile: rows are 44px touch targets with no gap between them. The label is fluid, `clamp(27px, (100vw − 40px) / 10, 38px)`: 28px at 320, 35px at 390, 38px at 430, with 1em leading and -1% tracking, so the full email stays on one line inside the 20px gutters. Superscripts use 0.01em tracking.
3. **Base bar**: pinned to the bottom, 20px up. Two equal columns with a 40px gap: availability left; link list (LinkedIn, Resume, Cosmos, GitHub) starting at the page midpoint + 20px, ©year right. On mobile the availability label is hidden.

Spacing: the eyebrow sits 20px from the top; the first row starts 30px below it (36px on phone). The email row is taller than the rest (85px desktop, 72px tablet, a Framer fixed height). The last row ends **120px above the bottom edge**, and the base bar sits inside that space with its labels 35px up. With four rows the block is content height: 548px on desktop, 505px on tablet and 369px on a 390px phone (at least 50vh / 40vh on desktop / tablet).

## Usage

- The footer is the only large Forest Green block outside the boot loader. Always `data-surface="green"`.
- The email reads as `MICAH.HOANG` with `@HEY.COM` as its superscript, so the display line stays one word.
- Keep exactly four contact lines, in this order. Availability text reflects real status; change it when it changes.

## API

| Class | Element | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mh-footer` | `footer` | Add `data-surface="green"`; 120px below the last row; `min-height: var(--mh-footer-min-height)` |
| `mh-footer__eyebrow` | `p.mh-label` | Small Mono, 130% leading |
| `mh-footer__contacts` | `ul` | Vertical list, 12px apart (no gap on mobile) |
| `mh-footer__contact` | `a` | Display Footer type; `sup` child is the mono tag; 44px min height on mobile |
| `mh-footer__bar` | `div` | Pinned near the bottom inside the 120px; 2 equal columns, 40px gap; children: availability, link list, ©year |

## Accessibility

- The `sup` text is part of the link name ("micah.hoang @hey.com"). Make sure the `href` matches (`mailto:`).
- Cream on Forest Green is about 12:1 contrast, fine at every size.

## Framer mapping

- Home renders this as the page section `SectionCta` plus the `FooterWhite*` bar; case studies use the **Footer** component. On tablet the Home contact rows render in GT Standard Medium; elsewhere they're Regular. That inconsistency is live; this system documents the Regular treatment.
- Mobile rules (fluid size, 44px rows, 20px gutters, Optro's legacy `Row` layers) live in `NavigationScrollGuard` (`Wnd19lx`), pinned by `ResumeAssetHost` (`xDqfenf`). 

- Native **Footer** component with desktop/tablet/phone variants (`FooterWhiteDesktop`, ...).
- The large contact words are a per-letter `MagText` component; the base-bar social labels use Text Flip Up (`p7tSTaD`), the same 420ms flip as every other link.
- Year: `FooterCopyrightYear` (`BF2H03E`).
- `ResumeAssetHost` (`xDqfenf`) is mounted invisibly inside the footer. It supplies the resume file and hosts the global helpers (`ParagraphPrettyWrap`, `NavigationScrollGuard`). **Never remove it from the footer.**

## Don't

- Don't add a sitemap, newsletter form or social icons.
- Don't put the footer on Cream.

<!-- content/components/hero.md -->

title: Hero
section: Components
order: 9
description: The opening of a page. A huge name and descriptor on Home; a bold title continuing in Stroke Gray on case studies.
status: live
framer: Home "Header" section (Heading 1 + Heading 3); case-study hero (Heading 2 Bold, two colors)
classes: [mh-hero, mh-hero__name, mh-hero__descriptor, mh-hero__bar, mh-hero__continuation]

# Hero

## Examples

### Home

```html example
<header class="mh-hero">
  <h1 class="mh-hero__name mh-text-display-xl">
    <span class="mh-reveal" style="--i:0"><span>Micah Hoang</span></span>
  </h1>
  <p class="mh-hero__descriptor mh-text-heading">
    <span class="mh-reveal" style="--i:1"><span>Brand designer with</span></span>
    <span class="mh-reveal" style="--i:2"><span>a systems mind.</span></span>
  </p>
  <div class="mh-hero__bar">
    <ul class="mh-link-list mh-label">
      <li><a class="mh-link" href="#"><span class="mh-flip"><span class="mh-flip__track"><span>LinkedIn</span><span aria-hidden="true">LinkedIn</span></span></span></a></li>
      <li><a class="mh-link" href="#"><span class="mh-flip"><span class="mh-flip__track"><span>Resume</span><span aria-hidden="true">Resume</span></span></span></a></li>
      <li><a class="mh-link" href="#"><span class="mh-flip"><span class="mh-flip__track"><span>Email</span><span aria-hidden="true">Email</span></span></span></a></li>
      <li><a class="mh-link" href="#"><span class="mh-flip"><span class="mh-flip__track"><span>Cosmos</span><span aria-hidden="true">Cosmos</span></span></span></a></li>
    </ul>
    <span class="mh-label">©2026</span>
  </div>
</header>
```

### Case study

```html example
<header class="mh-hero" data-variant="case-study">
  <h1 class="mh-hero__name">
    Gaia
    <span class="mh-hero__continuation">Turning noticing into a way of caring for the living world.</span>
  </h1>
</header>
```

## Usage

| Variant | Title | Supporting text | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Home | Display XL, bold, the name | Heading, two lines, Forest Green | `/` only |
| Case study | Display L, bold, project name | Same size and weight, continues in Stroke Gray | `/case-studies/*` |

- **Home**: the name sits in normal flow on the 20px gutter, its line box 100px from the top (101px on phone) under the fixed nav, at 100% leading: 120 / 94px, and on phones `min(58px, (100vw − 40px) / 6.2)` so it always fits the screen (it can wrap as a last resort). The descriptor follows directly (220 / 194 / 158px from the top), at a fixed width that breaks it over two lines (382 / 254 / 231px). The link row sits 10px above the hero's bottom edge: 16.9px links centered in an 18.9px row on desktop/tablet, 44px touch targets on phone. There is no rule here: the rule that follows belongs to the Selected work [Section Header](section-header.md).
- **Case study**: the project name is the start of a sentence that continues in muted gray: name, then one line of what the project does for people. Up to three lines on desktop. The full-bleed hero media and the [Meta Grid](meta-grid.md) follow.
- Hero copy rises in with the type reveal (900ms, 90ms stagger).

## API

| Class / attribute | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `mh-hero` | Column stack, 144px top padding |
| `data-variant="case-study"` | Applies Display L to `.mh-hero__name` |
| `mh-hero__name` | The `h1`. Add `mh-text-display-xl` for Home |
| `mh-hero__descriptor` | Heading style, `max-width: 11em` to force the two-line break |
| `mh-hero__continuation` | Muted continuation inside the case-study `h1` |
| `mh-hero__bar` | Base row with bottom rule |

## Accessibility

- One `h1` per page: the name on Home, the project name + continuation on case studies (read as one sentence).
- Reveal spans don't change reading order.

## Framer mapping

- Home: text styles **Heading 1** (name) and **Heading 3** (descriptor). Appear effects: name `translateY 110px → 0`, descriptor `90px → 0`, Snappy; replays are coordinated by `PageTransition` (`gmalnRr`).
- Case study: **Heading 2 Bold** in two text layers (`/Colors/Forest Green` then `/Colors/Stroke Gray`) or one rich-text layer with a color span.

## Don't

- Don't add a hero image to Home; the selected-work grid is the imagery.
- Don't put a subtitle under a case-study title. The continuation is the subtitle.
